title: UK Hospitals Test Five-Day Radiotherapy For Breast Cancer Treatment
summary: Thirty-nine UK hospitals are testing a five-day breast cancer radiotherapy treatment that could save patients ten hospital trips, Punch reports.
paragraphs: Dozens of medical centers across the United Kingdom are currently participating in a major study evaluating a shorter radiotherapy treatment for breast cancer patients. According to Punch, thirty-nine hospitals are taking part in the clinical trial to see if therapy can be reduced from three weeks to five days.

The research, known as the FAST-Forward Boost trial, is managed by the Institute of Cancer Research in London. It explores whether combining a five-day radiotherapy schedule with an extra targeted dose effectively prevents cancer from returning. The UK Department of Health indicated this change could spare patients ten trips to the hospital.

Over one thousand individuals have already joined the study, which aims to register more than four thousand eight hundred participants by 2028. Researchers plan to monitor patients for five years after treatment, with final results from the government-funded project expected to be released in 2033.
